harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Brought node1's previously-unconfigured lan-b-facing NIC (vtnet2) into service as its own OPNsense zone (opt2/LANB, 10.10.20.1/24) with a default-deny-safe pass rule, and gave node3's corresponding interface (enp8s0) a persistent static address (10.10.20.2/24) via systemd-networkd. Diagnostics (pf ruleset inspection, pfctl -d fault-isolation test, and per-interface tcpdump) showed node1's lan-a-facing NIC (vtnet1, paired with node2's enp8s0) was also unassigned in config.xml, so it was brought up the same way as zone opt1/LANA (10.10.10.1/24, node2 at 10.10.10.2/24) with a static route on node2/node3 pointing at node1 for the other zone's subnet — this was necessary for node3 to actually reach node2 through node1 as the task required, since neither zone had any pre-existing configuration. Verified node3 reaches node1 on lan-b and reaches node2 on lan-a via node1 (ttl=63 confirms routing through the gateway), bidirectionally. Then ran the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured healthy baselines (boot IDs / kern.boottime, interface addresses, live pings) on all three nodes, restarted node2, node3, and node1 one at a time (never concurrently), confirmed each node's boot identity changed (uuid/boottime + uptime reset), and re-verified full zone connectivity and pf rule persistence after each restart, ending with a final full topology check.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD) interfaces, config.xml, and pf ruleset; inspected node2/node3 Linux interfaces and systemd-networkd config
Used pfctl -d fault isolation plus per-interface tcpdump/STP bridge-id comparison to determine vtnet1<->node2:enp8s0 (lan-a) and vtnet2<->node3:enp8s0 (lan-b) physical mappings
Edited /conf/config.xml on node1 via a Python script (with .bak backup) to assign opt1 (LANA, vtnet1, 10.10.10.1/24) and opt2 (LANB, vtnet2, 10.10.20.1/24), each with a pass-any firewall rule
Applied changes with configctl interface reconfigure opt1/opt2 and configctl filter reload; confirmed pfctl -s rules shows the new pass rules and interface addresses

Configured persistent static addressing + cross-zone static routes on node2 (10.10.10.2/24) and node3 (10.10.20.2/24) via new /etc/systemd/network/10-enp8s0-*.network files, applied with networkctl reload/reconfigure
Verified node3<->node1 (lan-b) and node3<->node2 (lan-a, routed through node1, ttl=63) connectivity bidirectionally
Captured pre-restart baseline evidence (boot_id/kern.boottime, interface state, live pings) on all three nodes
Restarted node2, then node3, then node1 sequentially (one at a time, acknowledgement returned before disconnect), polled each until exec access returned
Confirmed changed boot identity on each node (new /proc boot_id or new kern.boottime + uptime reset)
Re-verified post-restart recovery of interface addresses, routes, pf rules, and end-to-end connectivity after each restart, finishing with a full-topology recheck

evidence.requirement: node1 lan-b interface identified and brought into service as its own zone with an address
evidence.summary: config.xml originally had no opt interfaces; script added opt1/opt2; configctl interface reconfigure applied 10.10.10.1/24 and 10.10.20.1/24 to vtnet1/vtnet2, confirmed via ifconfig showing descriptions LANA (opt1) and LANB (opt2)

evidence.requirement: Correct physical mapping of node1's interfaces to node2/node3 was verified before configuring (not assumed)
evidence.summary: pfctl -d fault isolation test proved vtnet1 reaches node2:enp8s0 and vtnet2 reaches node3:enp8s0 (opposite pairing failed), confirming lan-a/lan-b topology

evidence.requirement: Firewall (default-deny pf) explicitly permits the new zone traffic
evidence.summary: Default catch-all block-drop rule for unassigned interfaces was identified; after assigning opt1/opt2 and reloading filter, pass-in-quick rules for vtnet1/vtnet2 networks are active in pfctl -s rules
node3 pings node1's lan-b address 10.10.20.1 successfully (ttl=64, directly connected)

evidence.requirement: node3 reaches node2 on lan-a through node1 (routing)
evidence.summary: node3 pings node2's lan-a address 10.10.10.2 with ttl=63 (one router hop through node1); reverse direction from node2 to node3 also succeeds with ttl=63
Pre-restart kern.boottime=1788630332, pf enabled, both zone addresses present

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect, boot identity changed, and post-restart recovery verified
evidence.summary: Reboot command returned 'Connection to ... closed by remote host' as ack; kern.boottime changed to 1788630925 with uptime 6s; zone IPs, pf pass rules for vtnet1/vtnet2 all persisted after reboot; node3 successfully re-pings node1 (lan-b) and node2 (lan-a via node1) post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, changed boot identity, and recovery verified
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id c96a02ae...; reboot ack via stream closure; post-restart boot_id changed to ee7bd885... with uptime '0 min'; enp8s0 static config and routes persisted, ping to node1 and node3 succeeded after reboot

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, changed boot identity, and recovery verified
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 1e0cb179...; reboot ack via stream closure; post-restart boot_id changed to 16cc403d... with uptime '0 min'; enp8s0 static config and routes persisted, ping to node1 (lan-b) and node2 (lan-a via node1) succeeded after reboot
